record.paper_title: Open Problems Related to Quantum Query Complexity
record.context_brief: Relativization of blind and verified quantum-computation protocols
record.original_question: Are the protocols for blind and verified quantum computation due to Broadbent et al., Aharonov et al., and Mahadev inherently non-relativizing, or are there variants of these protocols that work relative to arbitrary oracles?

evidence.quote: Problem 9 Are the celebrated protocols for blind and verified quantum computation, due to Broadbent et al. [23], Aharonov et al. [11], and Mahadev [41], inherently non-relativizing?
Certainly these protocols don’t manifestly work relative to arbitrary oracles, but are there variants of the protocols that do?

artifact.status_search_result: No source resolving the relativization status of the Broadbent–Fitzsimons–Kashefi, Aharonov–Ben-Or–Eban–Mahadev, or Mahadev protocols was found. Related work (e.g., succinct blind quantum computation in the random-oracle model by Zhang, 2020) addresses succinctness under random oracles but does not resolve whether these verification protocols admit oracle-relative variants or are inherently non-relativizing. The question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Succinct Blind Quantum Computation Using a Random Oracle
status_evidence.snippet: Studies how a random oracle changes the complexity of universal blind quantum computation, but does not address general relativization of verified delegation protocols.
status_evidence.claim: Related but does not resolve whether the protocols are inherently non-relativizing.

status_evidence.title: Complexity-Theoretic Limitations on Blind Delegated Quantum Computation
status_evidence.snippet: Provides complexity-theoretic limitations and some oracle separations for blind delegated quantum computation, but does not settle the relativization question for the named protocols.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the open problem is reported.
